newsitem.title: INDIA: ICICI launches India's first index bond.
newsitem.headline: ICICI launches India's first index bond.

text.p: The Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICIC) said it was launching India's first bond with returns linked to a stock market index.
The index bond seeks to give the investor both the security of a debt instrument and the potential upside of the stock market, ICICI officials told a news conference on Monday.
ICICI is a leading term-lending bank.
Priced at 6,000 rupees, this bond comes with a detachable warrant. At the end of 12 years, the investor would receive 22,000 rupees for the bond.

Against the warrant, the investor would receive an amount equivalent to the value of the benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) 30-share index at the time, assuming a notional investment of 2,000 rupees, ICICI officials said.
Kundapur V. Kamath, ICICI managing director, said the index bonds could be a better alternative to mutual funds.
"Considering the cost of transactions in small amounts, the performance of mutual funds net of costs is below the index - internationally," Kamath said.
Kalpana Morparia, ICICI's general manager, said the index bond was targeted at the small investor.

Nimesh Kampani, chief of JM Financial and Investment Consultancy, said a small investor would require 2.3 million rupees to have a marketable lot of investment in the 30 firms comprising the BSE index.
The bonds would be listed and investors could exit whenever they thought the index was heading southwards, Kampani said.
ICICI is also offering improved versions of deep discount bond, encash bond, capital gains bond and regular income bond.
The public issue of unsecured redeemable debentures is targeting 7.50 billion rupees, with a right to retain oversubscription of an equal amount.
The issue has been given the highest rating by three Indian credit rating agencies -- CRISIL, CARE and ICRA.
The issue opens on March 31 and closes on April 28.
